chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, Zurarah ibn A'yan, Bukayr ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah al-'Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah عليهما السلام said: “The time of Zuhr after zawal is two qadam, and the time of 'Asr after that is two qadam; and this is the earliest time, until four aqdam pass for 'Asr.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: four measured intervals indicating the extent of the earliest period mentioned
key_terms.أَوَّلُ: the earliest or initial part of a prescribed time
key_terms.قَدَمَانِ: a measure used here to indicate a defined interval of time
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the designated time or period for an act of worship
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the middle of the sky; solar noon passing
key_terms.ٱلظُّهْرِ: the noon salat prayed after the sun passes the meridian

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the beginning of the times for Zuhr and 'Asr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the earliest portions of the times for Zuhr and 'Asr salat. It explains that after zawal, a measured interval is assigned to Zuhr, then another to 'Asr, indicating the structured commencement of their prayer times.
